nativeOwner.component: Codex parent decomposition with native V2 children

scenario.input: A synthetic repository and accepted plan packet defining three disjoint implementation slices, one dependent integration slice, exact write sets, and deterministic child result packets.
steps: Require the parent to state settled decisions, unresolved decision-changing questions, dependency order, and write-set ownership.
Start the three disjoint slices concurrently through native V2 children.
Start the integration slice only after all required child packets settle, then inspect write ownership and task chronology.

expectedObservableOutcomes: Disjoint child implementation intervals overlap without write-set collision.
The dependent integration slice waits for exact settled packets.
The final parent packet names changed paths, decisions, tests, unresolved defects, tree digest, and released write sets.
negativeAssertions: No fixed child count, Coding orchestrator, or broad repository tour is introduced.
No child rereads the complete plan when scoped refs are supplied.
No child edits a shared or dependent write set before ownership transfers.

baselineState.gap: Native child lifecycle controls exist, but no synthetic behavior repository proves decision-first exploration, parallel write sets, and dependent integration.

nativeOwner.component: native managed-worktree setup and Coding admission

scenario.input: A synthetic Coding repository whose trusted worktree setup cannot provide one required lockfile-local test binary.
steps: Create the managed worktree through native admission.
Run setup and verify the required package manager, lockfile, local binaries, links, and writable cache paths.
Inspect task, session, Codex app-server, and provider records after setup fails.

expectedObservableOutcomes: Admission fails with one native setup result before a Coding thread starts.
The task remains a truthful environment failure.
A clean new worktree is removed only through native ownership rules.
negativeAssertions: No provider call, Codex thread, V2 child, or model-authored repair begins.
Environment failure is not converted into static-evidence success.
No copied dependency layout or custom test runner is used.

baselineState.gap: Worktree cleanup controls exist, but missing toolchain admission is not yet proved across every Coding inference surface.

nativeOwner.component: native Workbench and installed package resolution

scenario.input: A synthetic workspace package whose installed dependency is reachable through an in-root symlink and exports one known API absent from the caller source tree.
steps: Give the explorer one API-existence question and exact package roots.
Resolve the installed package root through workspace and symlink metadata.
Return search coverage, read errors, exact export symbol, and supported implementation decision.

expectedObservableOutcomes: The explorer finds the installed API through the symlinked in-root package.
Its packet identifies the actual package root, symbol, and inspected coverage.
The implementation selects the existing API rather than creating a substitute.
negativeAssertions: An incomplete source-only search cannot claim the API is absent.
Workbench does not follow a symlink outside the allowed root.
No custom replacement is proposed while the installed native surface exists.

baselineState.gap: Workbench path safety has controls, but a positive symlinked installed-API discovery fixture is missing.

nativeOwner.component: native selected-shard test router and aggregate validation ledger

scenario.input: Three deterministic selected shards over one frozen tree: the first exits nonzero, and the later two write unique completion markers and settle independently.
steps: Dispatch all selected shards through the existing native test router.
Retain command identity, cwd, profile, start, end, exit status, output ref, and tree digest for each shard.
Return one aggregate defect ledger after every safe shard settles.

expectedObservableOutcomes: The first failure remains visible after later successes.
Both later safe shards run and produce their markers.
The aggregate ledger contains every shard status bound to the same tree digest.
negativeAssertions: A later success does not overwrite an earlier failure.
Environment failure does not become permission to substitute static evidence.
No second runner, command language, or fail-fast wrapper is added.

baselineState.gap: The router is tested, but selected-shard continuation and one aggregate digest-bound defect ledger are not frozen together.

nativeOwner.component: Codex validation and review packet identity

scenario.input: A synthetic repository at tree A with two independent review scopes, followed by one file mutation producing tree B.
steps: Bind validation and review packets to tree A and their declared file or dependency scopes.
Mutate one file covered by only one packet and compute tree B.
Project current and stale packet status to the Codex parent.

expectedObservableOutcomes: The affected packet becomes stale against tree B.
The unaffected packet remains current with its original digest and scope.
The parent cannot issue final approval until every material affected packet is current.
negativeAssertions: Review never approves a moving worktree.
Unrelated packets are not invalidated merely because the tree changed.
No full rerun is triggered without scope or dependency impact.

baselineState.gap: Codex event packets expose activity, but no exact tree A to tree B fixture proves selective review invalidation.

nativeOwner.component: native Codex V2 child lifecycle and process ownership

scenario.input: Two native V2 children: one settles then receives a follow-up turn, and one is cancelled while active with owned MCP and shell process fixtures.
steps: Settle the first child and reopen it through native follow-up.
Cancel the second child and archive or unsubscribe both through native Codex lifecycle.
Inspect task, child, process, write-set, and final settlement readback.

expectedObservableOutcomes: The reopened child is active and visible until its follow-up turn settles.
The cancelled child settles cancelled and its owned processes terminate.
Final Coding settlement shows no active or queued child and every write set released.
negativeAssertions: A reopened child does not edit under a completed task projection.
No MCP, browser, shell, app-server child process, or subscription survives settlement.
No process sweeper daemon is introduced.

baselineState.gap: Monitor, mirror, notification, and projection controls exist, but no assembled reopen, cancel, archive, process-settlement fixture exists.

nativeOwner.component: package-owned Codex purpose agents and parent review adjudication

scenario.input: A broad synthetic diff containing independent architecture, native-fit, validation, and code-correctness defects plus one fatal interaction across two lenses.
steps: Have the parent name only verdict-changing uncertainties.
Dispatch the existing package-owned specialist roles selectively with the exact diff digest and lens-specific scope.
Return compact packets and require the parent to adjudicate their interaction and issue the only final verdict.

expectedObservableOutcomes: Only material specialist lenses are selected.
Each packet binds the exact diff digest and reports its bounded scope.
The parent catches the fatal cross-lens interaction and rejects the diff.
negativeAssertions: No fixed panel, vote, duplicate broad inspection, or home-owned review-agent catalog appears.
Specialist pass results do not mechanically produce approval.
Minor reversible details do not trigger another specialist without a verdict-changing claim.

baselineState.gap: Purpose-agent assets exist, but no behavior fixture proves selective dispatch and parent-owned cross-lens adjudication.

scenario.input: A narrow synthetic one-file change with complete focused tests, no architecture or dependency change, and no material unresolved uncertainty.
steps: Have the parent classify the change, accepted decision, write set, validation, and remaining uncertainty.
Require it to decide whether any specialist can change severity or verdict.
Complete review and settlement using only the parent when no such claim exists.

expectedObservableOutcomes: The parent correctly selects no helper agents.
The final verdict binds the exact diff and focused validation evidence.
The packet explains why specialist review would have no material decision value.
negativeAssertions: No fixed specialist minimum or mandatory review sequence is applied.
Diff size alone does not determine whether helpers are used.
The parent does not perform extra source reads after all material claims are settled.

baselineState.gap: Review contracts exist, but there is no clean control proving that no specialist is the correct native decision.
